hook.text: Flynn Restaurant Group owns 2,400 restaurants across 6 brands. One franchisee, $4 billion in sales.

buildup.text: Multi-unit franchisees operate dozens or hundreds of locations, creating economies of scale within the system.

discovery.text: They share managers, negotiate supplier deals, and spread overhead across many units.

twist.text: Multi-unit operators have leverage over franchisors. Losing a 100-store operator is a major revenue event.

climax.text: 75% of new franchise locations go to existing multi-unit operators, not first-time buyers.

punchline.text: 2,400 restaurants, one owner. Franchising consolidation is accelerating.

quiz.question: What percentage of new franchise locations go to multi-unit operators?

details.summary: Multi-unit franchisees own and operate multiple franchise locations, often 10 to 100 or more. They achieve economies of scale in management, purchasing, and operations that single-unit owners cannot, and they now control over 50 percent of all franchise units in the United States.
details.whyItMatters: Multi-unit ownership has transformed franchising from small business ownership to corporate portfolio management. Understanding this trend reveals why franchisors increasingly prefer dealing with larger operators and how this shifts power dynamics.
takeaways: Multi-unit operators own over 50 percent of all franchise units in the US
Economies of scale in management and purchasing improve per-unit profitability
Franchisors prefer multi-unit operators for faster growth and operational consistency

faq.question: What advantages do multi-unit franchisees have over single-unit owners?
faq.answer: Lower costs through bulk purchasing, shared management overhead, training efficiencies, stronger negotiating position with the franchisor, ability to transfer best practices between locations, and diversification of risk across multiple units and sometimes multiple brands.

faq.question: How do multi-unit operators typically grow their portfolio?
faq.answer: They start with one or two units to learn the system, then sign area development agreements committing to opening multiple locations over a set timeline. Many also acquire existing locations from retiring single-unit owners. Some diversify across multiple franchise brands.
